title: My favourite hobby
paragraphs: My name is Samal Nurova. I am 18 years old and I am from Karaganda. I study Psychology at WKU in Uralsk. I have many interests, but my absolute favourite hobby is photography. I take photos every single day — in the morning, between classes, in the evenings, and on weekends. My camera is always with me. Photography is not just a hobby for me — it is the way I see and understand the world.

My camera is a Canon DSLR — my father gave it to me as a birthday present when I was 16. At first, I did not know how to use it properly. I watched online tutorials every evening for two months and practised every weekend. Now I understand aperture, shutter speed, and lighting. My father says that I am already a better photographer than him! I take great care of my camera — it is my most valuable possession.

I love to photograph landscapes and nature. The steppe around Uralsk is incredibly beautiful, especially in the early morning when the light is soft and golden. I wake up at 6 am on Saturdays and Sundays to take photos of the sunrise. The Ural River at dawn is one of my favourite subjects. I also love to photograph the WKU campus — the main building looks like a palace when the sun is behind it.

I also love portrait photography — taking photos of people. My classmates are my favourite subjects because they are natural and relaxed around me. I photograph them studying in the library, eating lunch in the cafeteria, playing sports, and laughing together. I believe that the best portraits capture a real moment — not a fake smile for the camera. I always say: "Forget I am here, and I will take your best photo."

Every week, I choose my three best photos and post them on my Instagram page. My account is called @samal_sees_world. I currently have more than 1,400 followers — mostly students from WKU and photographers from Karaganda. Sometimes professional photographers comment on my photos and give me advice. Their feedback helps me improve my technique and develop my own style.

Photography teaches me many important life skills. Patience — because the perfect moment does not always come quickly. Attention — because I notice small details that other people miss. Creativity — because every photo is a composition, a decision about colour, light, and angle. And confidence — because I show my work to thousands of people online. These skills help me in my Psychology studies too!

My biggest dream is to organise a solo photo exhibition at WKU before I graduate. I want to display 30 large prints on the walls of the main hall and invite all students and teachers. The theme will be "WKU Through My Eyes" — all photos taken on the campus and in the city of Uralsk. I already have more than 200 photos saved for this project.

If you love photography, my advice is simple: start today. You do not need an expensive camera — your phone camera is enough to begin. The most important thing is to look — really look — at the world around you. Notice the light, the shadows, the expressions on people's faces. Photography changes how you see everything. And once you start seeing the world through a camera lens, you can never stop!

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: Samal, you always have your camera. What are you photographing today?

dialogue.speaker: Samal
dialogue.text: The library! Look — the light on the windows is perfect right now.

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: Wow, that's beautiful! How long have you been into photography?

dialogue.speaker: Samal
dialogue.text: Since I was 16. My dad gave me my Canon for my birthday. It changed my life!

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: Do you take photos every day? Even on weekdays?

dialogue.speaker: Samal
dialogue.text: Yes! I always carry my camera. I take at least 50 photos a day.

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: And you post them on Instagram? I saw your page — it's amazing!

dialogue.speaker: Samal
dialogue.text: Thank you! I have over 1,400 followers now. Sometimes pro photographers comment!

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: That's incredible! What is your favourite thing to photograph?

dialogue.speaker: Samal
dialogue.text: Sunrises on the steppe. I wake up at 6 am on weekends just for that light.

dialogue.speaker: Timur
dialogue.text: 6 am?! On a weekend? That is very dedicated! Do you have a dream project?

dialogue.speaker: Samal
dialogue.text: Yes — a photo exhibition at WKU! "WKU Through My Eyes." One day!
